readme.head:
AURA

AURA is a production-tested SRE agent platform you can deploy in minutes.

In this demo, AURA investigates a payment failure by correlating Mezmo traces and logs, Prometheus latency, and Kubernetes deployment history. Three specialist agents identify an N+1 regression introduced by productcatalogservice 1.13.2, recommend rolling back to 1.13.1, and provide recovery checks and engineering follow-up.

Quick Start · Integrations · Documentation · Roadmap · Explore · Community

Connect your stack through guided setup, and AURA's preconfigured team of agents starts investigating incidents using the models you already rely on. From there, customize existing agents or add new ones to fit your infrastructure and SRE workflows. AURA handles the guardrails, APIs, state management, streaming, failure handling, and observability needed to connect AI models to production tools within operator-defined boundaries. ## Proven in Production AURA began as Mezmo’s internal harness for operating our own SaaS. Our engineering and SRE teams still use it for production operations today, and teams outside Mezmo run AURA in their own production environments. AURA also powers thousands of agent sessions each month in Mezmo’s hosted observability platform. ## Quick Start Install AURA on Linux or macOS with the [install script](scripts/install.sh). It downloads published release artifacts and verifies their checksums. ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mezmo/aura/main/scripts/install.sh | bash ``` Create a ready-to-run local agent: ```bash aura init # Choose an LLM provider and initial model, and write the initial config file ``` Start the agent: ```bash aura ``` ## Why AURA - **Operate inside your own security boundary.** Run AURA in your infrastructure, including air-gapped and highly regulated environments, with control over model, tool, storage, and telemetry destinations. - **Define the entire agent system in reviewable TOML.** Keep models, specialist agent teams, per-agent prompts, tools, approval policies, and guardrails together in configuration that can be versioned and reviewed. - **Use different model providers without rebuilding workflows.** Run OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock, Gemini, Ollama, or OpenRouter; switch providers with a configuration change or assign different models to different roles. - **Put sensitive actions behind human approval.** Require webhook or in-conversation approval before configured tool calls execute, with denial, timeout, and transport failures handled fail-closed. - **Trace every model, tool, and orchestration decision.** Export [OpenTelemetry traces](https://docs.mezmo.com/aura/tracing-spans) for requests, LLM turns, tool calls, and multi-agent execution so each result can be investigated end to end. ## Extensible Runtime - **Connect tools and RAG.** Discover tools from compatible MCP servers over Streamable HTTP, SSE, or STDIO, and ground agents through Qdrant or AWS Bedrock Knowledge Bases. - **Build multi-agent workflows.** Coordinate specialist agent teams with dependency-aware task execution while parking oversized tool results on disk for selective retrieval. - **Add reusable Agent Skills.** Load task-specific [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) instructions and supporting files only when they are needed. - **Interoperate or embed.** Connect AURA with other agents over A2A or embed its Rust core directly in your application. - **Use existing clients and SDKs.** Serve agents through an OpenAI-compatible API so clients such as LibreChat and OpenWebUI work unchanged, or run them locally through the AURA CLI. ## Production Safety Production controls define an operator-managed boundary around AURA: - Runs in your infrastructure, including air-gapped environments when model providers and MCP servers are locally reachable. - AURA sends agent prompts and tool data to the model providers, MCP servers, approval services, storage backends, and tracing destinations you configure. Enabled client-side tools and STDIO processes can initiate additional network traffic unless system-level network policy prevents it. Mezmo CLI product telemetry is separately disclosed and controlled. - Sensitive tool calls can require explicit human approval. - Credentials supplied through environment variables or secret mounts remain outside prompts only when referenced from designated authentication fields; environment substitution in prompt-bearing fields places their values into model context. - Tool, model, and orchestration activity can be exported as [OpenTelemetry traces](https://docs.mezmo.com/aura/tracing-spans). See the complete [security and data-handling model](SECURITY.md), including telemetry defaults, permission boundaries, prompt-injection risks, and supply-chain verification. ## Integrations Through compatible [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) servers and built-in integrations, AURA agen

findings.title: Prompt caching is off by default for Claude and Bedrock agents, so long system prompts and tool lists are re-billed at full price every turn
findings.why: The Anthropic and Bedrock model settings have a prompt_caching switch that defaults to false, and the reference config ships it commented out. Agents here re-send a long system prompt, a tool list from MCP servers and conversation history each turn, which is the pattern caching serves. Adopting it means setting prompt_caching = true under the agent's llm block (workers inherit it). Anthropic's prices put a write above plain input, so it only pays when the prefix repeats within the cache lifetime. Prompts under the model's minimum length are silently not cached. On Bedrock, enable it only for models that support caching. Anthropic's listed prices: a cache read costs 0.1x the input price, 0.05x on Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5, and 0.025x on Fable 5.1. A write costs 1.25x for 5 minutes or 2x for 1 hour. The saving on this product depends on how often its prefix repeats, which code can't show.

findings.why: Cargo.toml:49 declares 0.12.0, released 18 Dec 2025. The latest is 3.8.0, released 26 Oct 2026. Its release notes list: stop SSE reconnects on permanent GET errors (3.8.0); follow same-origin 307/308 redirects in the default Streamable HTTP client (3.6.0). Nobody has measured these on this product. Its release notes add spec versions yours doesn't have: 2026-07-28 (3.0.0) and 2025-11-25 (1.5.0). Not a gain here, as written: cancel an abandoned tools/call, prompts/get or resources/read (3.6.0). crates/aura/src/mcp/client.rs already tracks in-flight requests and sends its own cancellation notifications (CancelledNotificationParam, CANCEL_NOTIFICATION_TIMEOUT). Not a gain here, as written: support OIDC ID-token subjects in enterprise exchange (3.7.0). Nothing in the code that uses this library mentions it. Cargo.toml:40 also carries its own rmcp feature, so that moves too. rmcp carries all of the product's MCP tool connections, and it sits several major versions behind the latest. Moving it is a real upgrade of the MCP client code, with its cancellation and progress handling, rather than a version bump, and the rig-core rmcp feature moves with it.

findings.why: claude-sonnet-4-20250514 was shut down on 15 Jun 2026. Announced on 14 Apr 2026. Named successor: claude-sonnet-5-5. claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 shuts down on 30 Nov 2026. Announced on 30 Sep 2026. Named successor: claude-sonnet-5-5. examples/minimal/openrouter.toml:22 asks OpenRouter for anthropic/claude-sonnet-4, the same model, and OpenRouter's model list no longer has it. Check before switching: "Sonnet 5.5 returns a 400 for tool_choice any or tool, thinking budgets, temperature, top_p, top_k and assistant prefill." This repo sets budget_tokens at examples/complete/reasoning-models.toml:71 and temperature at examples/complete/reasoning-models.toml:63. Check before switching to Claude Sonnet 5.5: "Forced tool use ( tool_choice types any and tool ) returns a 400 error." tool_choice isn't anywhere in this repo's code. The Anthropic minimal example, the reasoning-models example and the OpenRouter example send retired or retiring Claude Sonnet ids, so anyone copying them gets errors. Move them to claude-sonnet-5-5 (OpenRouter needs its current Sonnet id); the reasoning example's temperature and thinking budget will return a 400 there, so those settings must be reworked.

findings.title: gpt-4o and 1 more OpenAI model shut down on 14 Jan 2027
findings.why: gpt-4o shuts down on 14 Jan 2027. Named successor: gpt-6-luna. gpt-4o-mini shuts down on 14 Jan 2027. Named successor: gpt-6-luna. Check before switching: "Unless reasoning effort is none, gpt-6-luna rejects temperature, top_p and top_logprobs." This repo sets temperature at examples/multi-agent/writer.toml:23. gpt-4o is the built-in default in the config code, the Helm dev and prod values, and several examples, and gpt-4o-mini is in the math example, so these stop working when OpenAI shuts them down. Move them to gpt-6-luna; with function calling and temperature in use, reasoning effort must be set to none, and answer quality should be tested first.

held_back.thing: Load skills in the open Agent Skills format
held_back.reason: False alarm: the README says AURA already loads Agent Skills in the open SKILL.md format (a skill catalog in the prompt, with load_skill and read_skill_file tools), and the flagged line is only a skills log directory in a file store.

held_back.thing: OpenAI and Gemini prompt cache tips (stable text first)
held_back.reason: Both are on by default, and no changing value at the start of a long prompt is visible in the code shown.

held_back.thing: Anthropic 1-hour cache
held_back.reason: It only matters once basic caching is on, and the code shows no setting for the cache lifetime.

held_back.thing: OpenAI 12-hour prompt cache
held_back.reason: The code shows no setting for cache retention or cache key, and write costs more than plain input.

held_back.thing: Vercel AI SDK (ai, npm)
held_back.reason: It is a JavaScript library and AURA is Rust; the provider layer is already handled through the rig crates and switched by config.

held_back.thing: antirion open-source LLM gateway
held_back.reason: A gateway adds a network hop AURA doesn't need, since it already switches between OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock, Gemini, Ollama and OpenRouter directly.

held_back.thing: Netdata MCP server
held_back.reason: Netdata is a real vendor, but it's less widely recognised among SRE teams than the three chosen, so it was left out.

held_back.thing: Kubernetes MCP servers (mcp-k8s-ro, kubernetes-mcp-server)
held_back.reason: Kubernetes is already in the README's integrations list.

held_back.thing: Sakana: Fugu Max (OpenRouter)
held_back.reason: AURA already routes work through its own coordinator and worker agents, and OpenRouter is already a supported provider. Fugu's own orchestration would duplicate that, and the listing states no gain for this code.

held_back.thing: Schelling Add Forward (multi-agent coordination MCP server)
held_back.reason: It is a small third-party server for agent-to-agent coordination, and AURA's coordinator already plans and runs tasks across workers.

held_back.thing: Gateco (permission-aware retrieval)
held_back.reason: It is a Python package for access-controlled retrieval, not a replacement for the Qdrant or Bedrock Knowledge Base search this product already runs, and it would add a separate service to host.

held_back.thing: agentdb (vector memory for agents)
held_back.reason: It is a Node package, and the product already has vector search through Qdrant, Bedrock Knowledge Bases and an in-memory store.

held_back.thing: Jevgrep (code search CLI)
held_back.reason: It is a TypeScript tool for searching code, and this product searches runbooks and documents from a Rust codebase.

held_back.thing: SkillMD's MCP server (com.skillmd/skillmd)
held_back.reason: It searches and installs skills from a public registry. AURA already loads skills from local directories at the operator's own paths, so a third-party registry adds no job the product lacks.

held_back.thing: runx (governed runtime for agent skills)
held_back.reason: It runs skills inside its own runtime and overlaps with AURA's existing load_skill and read_skill_file tools, so it would add a competing layer.

held_back.thing: AgentDiet Deterministic A2A Broken-JSON Repair & Schema Validator
held_back.reason: It repairs malformed JSON, but the existing fallback parser already handles JSON, Hermes XML, Pythonic and Qwen XML tool calls in Rust. Sending text to an outside service adds a hop and a new dependency.

held_back.thing: agent-json-reliability
held_back.reason: It is a Python library for JSON repair, and this product is Rust, so it can't be imported. The existing fallback parser already covers the tool-call formats.

held_back.thing: Anthropic Token Counting API request size raised from 32 MB to 128 MB
held_back.reason: The code counts Claude tokens with a local approximation (ClaudeApproxCounter), not Anthropic's Token Counting API, so the larger request limit doesn't change anything here.

held_back.thing: sqz (context compression MCP server)
held_back.reason: It compresses context for coding agents rather than counting tokens, so it doesn't replace the per-provider counters in context_budget.rs.

held_back.thing: Marrow AI: Control Layer for AI Agents (approval gate and audit trail MCP server)
held_back.reason: AURA already has its own human-approval middleware that fails closed, and an outside approval server would duplicate it instead of adding a capability.

held_back.thing: Anthropic OpenTelemetry export in beta
held_back.reason: AURA already exports its own OpenTelemetry spans for LLM turns, tool calls and multi-agent runs, so the Claude Console export adds nothing for this product.
